notes.notes: Safe with anyone at any time of day. Say it when you walk into a small shop or a lift: silence comes across as rude.

examples.tl: Hallo, heeft u een tafel voor twee?
examples.en: Hello, do you have a table for two?

notes.notes: Casual and friendly, fine with people your own age and in most cafés. Also used for 'bye' among friends.

examples.tl: Hoi, alles goed?
examples.en: Hi, everything good?

notes.notes: Until noon. The g is a soft scrape in the throat. Often clipped to 'Morgen!'

examples.tl: Goedemorgen, ik heb een reservering.
examples.en: Good morning, I have a reservation.

notes.notes: From noon until about 6 pm. The standard opener with shop and museum staff.

examples.tl: Goedemiddag, twee kaartjes voor het museum, alstublieft.
examples.en: Good afternoon, two tickets for the museum, please.

notes.notes: From about 6 pm. 'Goedenacht' and 'welterusten' are only for going to bed.

examples.tl: Goedenavond, we hebben gereserveerd voor zeven uur.
examples.en: Good evening, we have a reservation for seven o'clock.

notes.notes: Works as hello and as goodbye. Leaving a shop you hear a drawn-out 'Daaag!'

examples.tl: Dag, tot morgen!
examples.en: Bye, see you tomorrow!

notes.notes: Said 'doo-ee'. Cheerful and casual; cashiers and bartenders use it with everyone.

examples.tl: Bedankt en doei!
examples.en: Thanks and bye!

notes.notes: The polite goodbye for staff and strangers, literally 'until seeing'.

examples.tl: Dank u wel en tot ziens!
examples.en: Thank you and goodbye!

notes.notes: Said by almost every cashier. In the evening: 'Fijne avond!' Answer with 'U ook!' or 'Jij ook!'

examples.tl: Alstublieft, uw bon. Fijne dag nog!
examples.en: Here you are, your receipt. Have a nice day!

notes.notes: The reply to 'Fijne dag!', 'Fijn weekend!' and 'Eet smakelijk!'

examples.tl: Fijne avond! — Dank u, u ook!
examples.en: Have a nice evening! — Thank you, you too!

notes.notes: Also said when handing something over: 'here you are'. Written a.u.b. on signs.

examples.tl: Een koffie, alstublieft.
examples.en: A coffee, please.

examples.tl: Alstublieft, uw kaartje.
examples.en: Here you are, your ticket.

notes.notes: The 'wel' adds warmth, not meaning. With people your own age: 'dank je wel'.

examples.tl: Dank u wel voor uw hulp.
examples.en: Thank you for your help.

notes.notes: Neutral: fits both u and je situations. 'Heel erg bedankt' = thanks very much.

examples.tl: Bedankt voor de tip!
examples.en: Thanks for the tip!

notes.notes: Literally 'gladly done'. You will also hear 'geen dank' and plain 'alsjeblieft'.

examples.tl: Dank u wel! — Graag gedaan.
examples.en: Thank you! — You're welcome.

notes.notes: The everyday apology, for bumping into someone or interrupting. For something serious: 'Het spijt me.'

examples.tl: Sorry, ik spreek niet zo goed Nederlands.
examples.en: Sorry, I don't speak Dutch very well.

notes.notes: To get someone's attention or to get past. Stress on the second syllable: par-DON.

examples.tl: Pardon, is dit de tram naar Centraal Station?
examples.en: Excuse me, is this the tram to Central Station?

notes.notes: Reply to 'sorry' or to a request. Also heard: 'geeft niks' (never mind).

examples.tl: Sorry, ik ben een beetje laat. — Geen probleem.
examples.en: Sorry, I'm a bit late. — No problem.

notes.notes: Said 'yah'. 'Ja hoor' is a friendly 'sure'.

examples.tl: Ja, dat klopt.
examples.en: Yes, that's right.

notes.notes: Said 'nay'. At Albert Heijn the cashier asks 'Heeft u een bonuskaart?': this is your answer.

examples.tl: Nee, ik heb geen bonuskaart.
examples.en: No, I don't have a loyalty card.

notes.notes: The natural way to accept an offer. A bare 'ja' sounds a bit flat.

examples.tl: Wilt u er slagroom bij? — Ja, graag.
examples.en: Would you like whipped cream with it? — Yes, please.

notes.notes: Careful: a bare 'dank u' in reply to an offer is usually taken as no. To accept, say 'ja, graag'.

examples.tl: Wilt u nog koffie? — Nee, dank u.
examples.en: Would you like more coffee? — No, thank you.

notes.notes: After an order it means 'please': 'Een thee, graag.' With a verb it means 'like to': 'Ik wil graag...'

examples.tl: Twee koffie, graag.
examples.en: Two coffees, please.

notes.notes: Used exactly as in English. 'Prima' = fine, great.

examples.tl: Oké, dan nemen we de volgende trein.
examples.en: Okay, then we'll take the next train.

notes.notes: Said 'khoot'. Also the reply 'fine, okay': 'Is dat goed?' 'Ja, goed.'

examples.tl: Het hotel is heel goed.
examples.en: The hotel is very good.

examples.tl: Is morgen om tien uur goed?
examples.en: Is tomorrow at ten okay?

notes.notes: Said 'na-TUUR-luk'. A warm yes to a request.

examples.tl: Mag ik hier zitten? — Ja, natuurlijk.
examples.en: May I sit here? — Yes, of course.

notes.notes: 'Ik snap het niet' is the casual version. 'Ik versta u niet' = I can't make out what you are saying.

examples.tl: Sorry, ik begrijp het niet. Kunt u het in het Engels zeggen?
examples.en: Sorry, I don't understand. Can you say it in English?

notes.notes: Nearly everyone does and many switch as soon as they hear an accent. Opening in Dutch first is still seen as good manners.

examples.tl: Goedemiddag, spreekt u Engels? — Ja hoor, natuurlijk.
examples.en: Good afternoon, do you speak English? — Sure, of course.

notes.notes: Languages are capitalized in Dutch: Nederlands, Engels.

examples.tl: Sorry, ik spreek geen Nederlands. Spreekt u Engels?
examples.en: Sorry, I don't speak Dutch. Do you speak English?

notes.notes: Said 'un BAY-chuh'. Works for amounts and for degree: 'een beetje moe' = a bit tired.

examples.tl: Ik spreek een beetje Nederlands.
examples.en: I speak a little Dutch.

notes.notes: A quick casual alternative is 'Sorry?' or 'Wat zegt u?' (what did you say?).

examples.tl: Sorry, kunt u dat herhalen? Ik verstond het niet.
examples.en: Sorry, can you repeat that? I didn't catch it.

accept: Can you speak a bit slower?
notes.notes: Langzaam = slow, langzamer = slower. 'Wat' here means 'a bit'.

examples.tl: Kunt u wat langzamer praten, alstublieft? Ik leer Nederlands.
examples.en: Can you speak a bit more slowly, please? I'm learning Dutch.

notes.notes: Point at the word on a menu or sign while you ask.

examples.tl: Wat betekent dit woord op de menukaart?
examples.en: What does this word on the menu mean?

notes.notes: The verb after 'ik' is the bare stem: ik ben, ik heb, ik wil, ik ga.

examples.tl: Ik ben toerist.
examples.en: I'm a tourist.

notes.notes: For staff, strangers and older people; the verb ends in -t (u bent, u heeft). Staff often say 'je' to you: normal, not rude.

examples.tl: Heeft u een momentje?
examples.en: Do you have a moment?

notes.notes: 'Jij' is the stressed form. Use it with people your own age in bars, hostels and at a race. Plural 'you all' = jullie.

examples.tl: Kom je ook uit Amerika?
examples.en: Are you from America too?

notes.notes: 'Dit' for het-words and for pointing at anything; 'deze' before de-words: deze trein, dit station.

examples.tl: Wat is dit?
examples.en: What is this?

examples.tl: Dit is mijn koffer.
examples.en: This is my suitcase.

notes.notes: 'Dat' for het-words and for pointing; 'die' before de-words: die tram, dat huis.

examples.tl: Dat is goed.
examples.en: That's fine.

examples.tl: Mag ik dat zien?
examples.en: May I see that?

notes.notes: Said like English 'here'. Opposite: daar (there).

examples.tl: Ik ben hier voor de marathon.
examples.en: I'm here for the marathon.

notes.notes: Said like the letter N. Not to be confused with 'een' (a / one).

examples.tl: Een koffie en een appeltaart, alstublieft.
examples.en: A coffee and an apple pie, please.

notes.notes: Trap: Dutch 'of' is English 'or'. English 'of' is 'van'.

examples.tl: Koffie of thee?
examples.en: Coffee or tea?

notes.notes: Comes after the verb and its object: 'Ik weet het niet.' Before a noun with no article, use 'geen' instead.

examples.tl: Ik weet het niet.
examples.en: I don't know.

examples.tl: De lift werkt niet.
examples.en: The elevator isn't working.

notes.notes: Also 'by' for transport: met de trein, met de fiets.

examples.tl: Een koffie met melk, alstublieft.
examples.en: A coffee with milk, please.

examples.tl: We gaan met de trein.
examples.en: We're going by train.

notes.notes: Handy for orders: zonder suiker (no sugar), zonder ui (no onion), zonder vlees (no meat).

examples.tl: Een broodje kaas zonder boter, alstublieft.
examples.en: A cheese sandwich without butter, please.

notes.notes: Also 'some / a bit': 'wat water' = some water.

examples.tl: Wat is dat?
examples.en: What is that?

examples.tl: Wat wilt u drinken?
examples.en: What would you like to drink?

notes.notes: Said to you by staff, or by you while you dig for your ticket or card.

examples.tl: Een momentje, alstublieft, ik zoek mijn kaartje.
examples.en: One moment, please, I'm looking for my ticket.

notes.notes: Polite way to address a man you do not know. Said 'muh-NAYR'. To a group: 'heren'.

examples.tl: Pardon, meneer, u vergeet uw tas.
examples.en: Excuse me, sir, you're forgetting your bag.

notes.notes: For any adult woman, married or not. Said 'muh-VROW'. To a group: 'dames'.

examples.tl: Dank u wel, mevrouw.
examples.en: Thank you, ma'am.

notes.notes: Polite: 'Hoe gaat het met u?' A short, honest answer is expected: 'Goed, dank je.'

examples.tl: Hé, hoe gaat het? — Goed, dank je.
examples.en: Hey, how are you? — Good, thanks.

notes.notes: With someone you address as u: 'Goed, en met u?'

examples.tl: Alles goed? — Ja, goed, en met jou?
examples.en: Everything good? — Yes, good, and you?

notes.notes: Literally 'how are you called?' Polite: 'Hoe heet u?'

examples.tl: Ik ben Mark. Hoe heet jij?
examples.en: I'm Mark. What's your name?

notes.notes: Swap in your own name. 'Ik ben ...' is just as common. First names are used straight away.

examples.tl: Hoi, ik heet Mark. Ik kom uit Amerika.
examples.en: Hi, my name is Mark. I'm from the US.

notes.notes: 'Waar ... vandaan' = where from; the 'vandaan' goes at the end.

examples.tl: Waar kom je vandaan? — Uit Amerika, maar ik woon in Manila.
examples.en: Where are you from? — From the US, but I live in Manila.

accept_tl: Ik kom uit de Verenigde Staten.
notes.notes: 'Amerika' is what people say; 'de Verenigde Staten' (de VS) is the formal name.

examples.tl: Ik kom uit Amerika, en jij?
examples.en: I'm from the US, and you?

notes.notes: Filipijnen takes 'de' (it is plural). Said 'fee-lee-PAY-nun'.

examples.tl: Ik woon in de Filipijnen, in Manila.
examples.en: I live in the Philippines, in Manila.

notes.notes: 'Voor mijn werk' = for work; 'voor de marathon' = for the marathon.

examples.tl: Ik ben hier een week op vakantie.
examples.en: I'm here on vacation for a week.

notes.tl: Het is mijn eerste keer in Nederland.
notes.en: It's my first time in the Netherlands.
accept: This is my first time in the Netherlands.
accept_tl: Dit is mijn eerste keer in Nederland.
notes.notes: Keer = time (occasion). Tweede keer = second time.

examples.tl: Het is mijn eerste keer in Nederland en ik vind het geweldig.
examples.en: It's my first time in the Netherlands and I love it.

notes.notes: 'Aangenaam' is the short formal version, said with a handshake.

examples.tl: Ik ben Mark. — Sanne. Leuk je te ontmoeten!
examples.en: I'm Mark. — Sanne. Nice to meet you!

notes.notes: 'Ik vind ... leuk / mooi / lekker' = I like ... (fun / beautiful / tasty). The opinion word goes last.

examples.tl: Ik vind Amsterdam heel leuk, vooral de grachten.
examples.en: I really like Amsterdam, especially the canals.

notes.notes: True of nearly everyone; a nice thing to say when someone apologizes for their English.

examples.tl: Je Engels is heel goed! — Dank je, we leren het al vroeg op school.
examples.en: Your English is very good! — Thanks, we learn it early at school.

accept: I'm learning a bit of Dutch.
notes.notes: People switch to English to be helpful, not to brush you off. Say 'Ik wil graag oefenen' (I'd like to practise) and they play along.

examples.tl: Ik leer een beetje Nederlands voor mijn reis.
examples.en: I'm learning a little Dutch for my trip.

notes.notes: Said 'prohst'. Look people in the eye as you clink glasses.

examples.tl: Proost! Op de marathon!
examples.en: Cheers! To the marathon!

notes.en: What do you do for work?
accept: What do you do for a living?
notes.notes: A normal small-talk question. Answer with 'Ik werk in ...' or 'Ik ben ...' plus the job, without an article.

examples.tl: Wat doe je voor werk? — Ik werk in de IT.
examples.en: What do you do for work? — I work in IT.

notes.notes: Blijven = to stay. Also asked at hotel reception and by border police.

examples.tl: Hoe lang blijf je in Nederland? — Tot maandag.
examples.en: How long are you staying in the Netherlands? — Until Monday.

notes.notes: Swap in: drie dagen, tot zondag (until Sunday), een paar dagen (a few days).

examples.tl: Ik blijf een week, en daarna ga ik naar België.
examples.en: I'm staying a week, and after that I'm going to Belgium.

notes.notes: 'Tot' + time = see you then: tot zondag, tot vanavond, tot volgende week.

examples.tl: Welterusten, tot morgen!
examples.en: Good night, see you tomorrow!

notes.notes: Means later today. 'Tot zo' = in a few minutes. 'Tot later' is open-ended.

examples.tl: Ik ga even douchen. Tot straks!
examples.en: I'm going to take a quick shower. See you later!

notes.notes: Said 'suuk-SES'. What everyone will wish you before the race. 'Veel succes!' = lots of luck.

examples.tl: Succes zondag met de marathon!
examples.en: Good luck with the marathon on Sunday!

notes.notes: Said 'vayl pluh-ZEER'. For any outing: a concert, a trip, a night out.

examples.tl: Gaan jullie naar het concert? Veel plezier!
examples.en: Are you going to the concert? Have fun!

notes.notes: Only when someone is going to bed. Leaving a bar at night you say 'fijne avond' or 'doei'.

examples.tl: Ik ga slapen. Welterusten!
examples.en: I'm going to bed. Good night!

notes.notes: Heard everywhere from Friday afternoon. 'Fijn' not 'fijne', because weekend is a het-word.

examples.tl: Tot maandag, fijn weekend!
examples.en: See you Monday, have a good weekend!

accept: Do you want something to drink?
Would you like something to drink?
notes.notes: Offering a drink. From a waiter you will hear 'Wilt u iets drinken?'

examples.tl: Wil je iets drinken? — Ja, lekker, een biertje.
examples.en: Would you like a drink? — Yes, great, a beer.

notes.notes: People take turns buying rounds ('rondjes'). 'Ik trakteer' = my treat.

examples.tl: Laat maar, dit rondje is van mij.
examples.en: Don't worry, this round is on me.

notes.notes: For activities, people and plans. 'Mooi' is for looks, 'lekker' for food. 'Wat leuk!' = how nice!

examples.tl: Wat leuk dat je de marathon loopt!
examples.en: How cool that you're running the marathon!

examples.tl: Het was een leuke avond.
examples.en: It was a fun evening.

notes.notes: The famous untranslatable word: warm, sociable, good company. A bar, an evening or a person can be gezellig.

examples.tl: Wat een gezellig café!
examples.en: What a cozy bar!

notes.notes: A man, or in general; a woman is 'Amerikaanse'. Adjective: Amerikaans. Plural: Amerikanen.

examples.tl: Ik ben Amerikaan, maar ik woon in Azië.
examples.en: I'm American, but I live in Asia.

notes.notes: Used without an article: 'in Nederland'. 'Holland' strictly means just the two western provinces.

examples.tl: Nederland is kleiner dan ik dacht.
examples.en: The Netherlands is smaller than I thought.

notes.notes: The language, and the adjective. A Dutch person is 'een Nederlander'.

examples.tl: Nederlands lijkt een beetje op Engels en Duits.
examples.en: Dutch is a bit like English and German.

notes.notes: Said 'va-KAN-see'. Plural: vakanties.

examples.tl: Waar ga je naartoe op vakantie?
examples.en: Where are you going on vacation?

notes.notes: 'Een vriend van mij' = a friend; 'mijn vriend' = my boyfriend. Female: vriendin. Plural: vrienden.

examples.tl: Ik reis met een vriend van mij.
examples.en: I'm travelling with a friend of mine.

notes.notes: To live somewhere: ik woon, u woont. 'To be alive' is 'leven'.

examples.tl: Waar woon je?
examples.en: Where do you live?

notes.notes: Said 'AHR-dukh'. For people and gestures. 'Dat is aardig van u' = that is kind of you.

examples.tl: Dat is heel aardig van u, dank u wel.
examples.en: That's very kind of you, thank you.

notes.notes: Relatives in the wide sense. Your own household of parents and children is 'het gezin'.

examples.tl: Mijn familie woont in Amerika.
examples.en: My family lives in the US.

notes.notes: Said 'ayn'. Written with accents when it is the number; unstressed 'een' ('un') is the article 'a'.

examples.tl: Eén kaartje, alstublieft.
examples.en: One ticket, please.

notes.notes: Said 'tway'. Drinks stay singular when you order by number: twee koffie, drie bier.

examples.tl: Twee koffie, alstublieft.
examples.en: Two coffees, please.

notes.notes: Said 'dree' with a rolled or throaty r.

examples.tl: Ik blijf drie nachten, tot vrijdag.
examples.en: I'm staying three nights, until Friday.

notes.notes: Said 'veer'. 'Met z'n vieren' = the four of us.

examples.tl: Een tafel voor vier personen, alstublieft.
examples.en: A table for four, please.

notes.notes: The 'ij' sounds close to the 'ay' in 'say', mouth a little more open: roughly 'vayf'.

examples.tl: De trein vertrekt over vijf minuten.
examples.en: The train leaves in five minutes.

notes.notes: Said 'zess', short e.

examples.tl: Het ontbijt begint om zes uur.
examples.en: Breakfast starts at six o'clock.

notes.notes: Said 'ZAY-vun'. On the phone and in announcements often 'zeuven' so it is not mixed up with 'negen'.

examples.tl: We eten om zeven uur.
examples.en: We're eating at seven o'clock.

notes.notes: The 'ch' is the throaty scrape, as in Scottish 'loch': 'akht'.

examples.tl: De trein naar Utrecht vertrekt van spoor acht.
examples.en: The train to Utrecht leaves from platform eight.

notes.notes: Said 'NAY-khun', with the throaty g.

examples.tl: Het museum gaat om negen uur open.
examples.en: The museum opens at nine o'clock.

notes.notes: Said 'teen'. 'Euro' stays singular after a number: tien euro.

examples.tl: Dat is tien euro.
examples.en: That's ten euros.

notes.notes: Said 'el-uf', almost two syllables.

examples.tl: Uitchecken kan tot elf uur.
examples.en: You can check out until eleven o'clock.

notes.notes: Then: dertien 13, veertien 14, vijftien 15, zestien 16, zeventien 17, achttien 18, negentien 19.

examples.tl: We lunchen om twaalf uur.
examples.en: We're having lunch at twelve o'clock.

notes.notes: Said 'TWIN-tukh'. Tens: dertig 30, veertig 40, vijftig 50, zestig 60, zeventig 70, tachtig 80, negentig 90.

examples.tl: Het kost twintig euro.
examples.en: It costs twenty euros.

notes.notes: Units first, then tens: 'one-and-twenty'. 35 = vijfendertig, 42 = tweeënveertig. Listen twice when prices are read out.

examples.tl: Uw kamer is nummer eenentwintig.
examples.en: Your room is number twenty-one.

notes.notes: Just 'honderd', never 'een honderd'. 150 = honderdvijftig. 1000 = duizend.

examples.tl: De kamer kost honderd euro per nacht.
examples.en: The room costs a hundred euros a night.

notes.notes: 'Hoe laat' (literally 'how late') = what time. 'Hoe laat begint het?' = what time does it start?

examples.tl: Hoe laat is het? — Het is bijna vier uur.
examples.en: What time is it? — It's almost four o'clock.

notes.notes: Stays singular after a number: drie uur = three o'clock or three hours. Timetables use the 24-hour clock (14.30 uur).

examples.tl: Het is drie uur.
examples.en: It's three o'clock.

examples.tl: De vlucht duurt twee uur.
examples.en: The flight takes two hours.

notes.notes: Trap: 'half' counts toward the NEXT hour. Half drie = 2:30, half negen = 8:30.

examples.tl: Het ontbijt is tot half elf.
examples.en: Breakfast is until 10:30.

notes.notes: Over = past. 'Tien over twee' = 2:10.

examples.tl: De trein vertrekt om kwart over twee.
examples.en: The train leaves at quarter past two.

notes.notes: Voor = to. Also: tien voor drie (2:50), vijf over half drie (2:35, 'five past half three').

examples.tl: Ik ben er om kwart voor drie.
examples.en: I'll be there at quarter to three.

notes.notes: Plural: minuten. Said 'mee-NUUT' with the tight Dutch uu.

examples.tl: De tram komt over twee minuten.
examples.en: The tram comes in two minutes.

notes.notes: Said 'vun-DAKH'.

examples.tl: Is het museum vandaag open?
examples.en: Is the museum open today?

notes.notes: Also 'morning' (de morgen). Morgenochtend = tomorrow morning; overmorgen = the day after tomorrow.

examples.tl: Morgen gaan we naar Utrecht.
examples.en: Tomorrow we're going to Utrecht.

notes.notes: Said with the tight Dutch u, like French 'tu'.

examples.tl: Kunnen we nu inchecken?
examples.en: Can we check in now?

notes.notes: Later today, not days from now. 'Zo' = in a minute; 'later' = some other time.

examples.tl: Ik kom straks terug.
examples.en: I'll come back later.

notes.notes: Vanochtend = this morning, vanmiddag = this afternoon, vannacht = tonight after bedtime (or last night).

examples.tl: Heeft u vanavond een tafel vrij?
examples.en: Do you have a table free tonight?

notes.notes: Plural: dagen (long a). 'Elke dag' = every day; 'de hele dag' = all day.

examples.tl: Ik blijf vier dagen in Amsterdam.
examples.en: I'm staying four days in Amsterdam.

notes.notes: Said 'vayk'. Plural: weken. Volgende week = next week, vorige week = last week.

examples.tl: We zijn hier een week.
examples.en: We're here for a week.

notes.notes: Days are not capitalized. 'Op maandag' = on Monday(s). Many museums and small shops are closed on Mondays.

examples.tl: Maandag vlieg ik terug naar Manila.
examples.en: On Monday I fly back to Manila.

notes.notes: Abbreviated 'di' on opening-hours signs (ma di wo do vr za zo).

examples.tl: Dinsdag gaan we naar de markt.
examples.en: On Tuesday we're going to the market.

notes.notes: Said 'WOONS-dakh': 'oe' is always 'oo'.

examples.tl: Woensdag komen we aan op Schiphol.
examples.en: On Wednesday we arrive at Schiphol.

notes.notes: 'Koopavond' (late shopping until 9 pm) is on Thursday in Amsterdam and many towns, Friday in others.

examples.tl: Op donderdag zijn de winkels tot negen uur open.
examples.en: On Thursdays the shops are open until nine.

notes.notes: Said 'VRAY-dakh'.

examples.tl: Vrijdag haal ik mijn startnummer op.
examples.en: On Friday I'm picking up my race bib.

notes.notes: The big shopping and market day; city centres are packed.

examples.tl: Zaterdag is het druk in de stad.
examples.en: On Saturday it's busy in town.

notes.notes: Shops in the big cities open around noon on Sunday; in small towns many stay closed.

examples.tl: De marathon is op zondag.
examples.en: The marathon is on Sunday.

notes.notes: For a clock time people usually ask 'hoe laat?' instead.

examples.tl: Wanneer vertrekt de boot?
examples.en: When does the boat leave?

notes.notes: Duren = to last / take (time). 'Hoe lang' = how long.

examples.tl: Hoe lang duurt de rondvaart? — Ongeveer een uur.
examples.en: How long does the canal cruise take? — About an hour.

notes.notes: 'Te laat' = too late / late for something. Opposite: vroeg (early).

examples.tl: Sorry dat ik te laat ben.
examples.en: Sorry I'm late.

notes.notes: Persoon, plural personen. 'Met z'n tweeën' = the two of us. For one: 'voor één persoon'.

examples.tl: Ik wil graag een tafel reserveren voor twee personen.
examples.en: I'd like to book a table for two.

notes.notes: Said 'op achttien oktober': plain number, day before month, months not capitalized. Written 18-10-2026.

examples.tl: Ik vertrek op 18 oktober.
examples.en: I'm leaving on October 18.

notes.notes: Plural: tafels. In cafés you usually seat yourself; in restaurants wait to be shown a table.

examples.tl: Heeft u een tafel bij het raam?
examples.en: Do you have a table by the window?

notes.notes: Usually just 'de kaart'. Careful: 'het menu' is a set meal of several courses.

examples.tl: Heeft u een Engelse menukaart?
examples.en: Do you have an English menu?

notes.notes: Said 'RAY-kuh-ning'. You have to ask for it: staff will not bring it unasked. Plural: rekeningen.

examples.tl: Kunnen we de rekening krijgen?
examples.en: Can we get the bill?

notes.notes: Said 'VAH-ter'. Tap water is 'kraanwater' and is excellent. Bottled: 'plat' (still) or 'bruisend / met prik' (sparkling).

examples.tl: Een fles water zonder prik, alstublieft.
examples.en: A bottle of still water, please.

notes.notes: A plain 'koffie' is a small black cup, often with a biscuit. Koffie verkeerd = latte.

examples.tl: Twee koffie en een cappuccino, alstublieft.
examples.en: Two coffees and a cappuccino, please.

notes.notes: Said 'tay'. 'Verse muntthee' (fresh mint tea) is on every café menu.

examples.tl: Een verse muntthee, alstublieft.
examples.en: A fresh mint tea, please.

notes.notes: Order 'een biertje': a small draft lager, about 25 cl. 'Van de tap' = on tap. 'Speciaalbier' = craft and Belgian styles.

examples.tl: Welk bier heeft u van de tap?
examples.en: Which beer do you have on tap?

notes.notes: Said 'vayn'. Rode wijn = red, witte wijn = white, huiswijn = house wine.

examples.tl: Een glas rode wijn, alstublieft.
examples.en: A glass of red wine, please.

notes.notes: A filled roll, the standard Dutch lunch: broodje kaas, broodje gezond (ham, cheese, salad). Plural: broodjes.

examples.tl: Een broodje kaas om mee te nemen, alstublieft.
examples.en: A cheese sandwich to take away, please.

notes.notes: Jong = young and mild, belegen = matured, oud = aged and sharp. Plural: kazen.

examples.tl: Mag ik de oude kaas proeven?
examples.en: May I taste the aged cheese?

notes.notes: The bar snack, served by the plate with mustard. The inside is molten hot: bite carefully. Plural: bitterballen.

examples.tl: Een portie bitterballen, alstublieft.
examples.en: A portion of bitterballen, please.

notes.notes: Two thin waffles glued with caramel syrup. Best warm from a market stall. Plural: stroopwafels.

examples.tl: Een verse stroopwafel van de markt is het lekkerst.
examples.en: A fresh stroopwafel from the market is the tastiest.

notes.notes: Plate-sized and thin, sweet or savoury (spek = bacon, kaas, appel). Plural: pannenkoeken. Poffertjes = mini pancakes.

examples.tl: Ik neem de pannenkoek met spek en stroop.
examples.en: I'll have the pancake with bacon and syrup.

notes.notes: 'Patat' in Amsterdam and the north, 'friet' in the south. The default sauce is mayonnaise.

examples.tl: Een grote friet met mayonaise, alstublieft.
examples.en: A large fries with mayonnaise, please.

notes.notes: Raw salted herring with onion and pickle from a street stall. 'Hollandse Nieuwe' is the new-season catch, from June.

examples.tl: Een haring met uitjes, alstublieft.
examples.en: A herring with onions, please.

notes.notes: Deep and chunky, served 'met slagroom' (with whipped cream).

examples.tl: Een appeltaart met slagroom en een koffie, graag.
examples.en: An apple pie with whipped cream and a coffee, please.

notes.notes: Kipsaté (chicken satay with peanut sauce) is on most café menus. Plural: kippen.

examples.tl: Ik neem de kipsaté met friet.
examples.en: I'll have the chicken satay with fries.

notes.notes: Said 'vlays'. Rundvlees = beef, varkensvlees = pork, gehakt = minced meat.

examples.tl: Ik eet liever vis dan vlees.
examples.en: I prefer fish to meat.

notes.notes: Plural: vissen. Kibbeling = battered fried fish chunks, sold at fish stalls.

examples.tl: Wat is de vis van de dag?
examples.en: What is the fish of the day?

notes.notes: Said 'vay-khuh-TAH-rees'. 'Vega' is the short form on menus; veganistisch = vegan.

examples.tl: Heeft u ook vegetarische gerechten?
examples.en: Do you also have vegetarian dishes?

notes.notes: The all-purpose word of approval: food, weather, a nap. 'Lekker!' on its own is fine.

examples.tl: De soep is erg lekker.
examples.en: The soup is very tasty.

notes.notes: Ik eet, wij eten; past: gegeten. 'Het eten' as a noun = the food.

examples.tl: Waar kunnen we hier goed eten?
examples.en: Where can we eat well around here?

notes.notes: Ik drink; past: gedronken. 'Iets drinken' = to have a drink.

examples.tl: Zullen we ergens iets gaan drinken?
examples.en: Shall we go and have a drink somewhere?

notes.notes: Ik bestel; past: besteld. In many cafés you order and pay at the bar, or by QR code on the table.

examples.tl: Kunnen we al bestellen?
examples.en: Can we order already?

notes.notes: From 'PIN code'. Also means taking cash out of an ATM. Many places are card-only.

examples.tl: Kan ik hier pinnen?
examples.en: Can I pay by card here?

notes.notes: Service is included. Rounding up or 5-10% for good table service is normal; nothing is expected at a counter.

examples.tl: Hoeveel fooi geef je hier meestal?
examples.en: How much do you usually tip here?

notes.notes: Grilled ham-and-cheese sandwich, on every café lunch menu, served with ketchup. Plural: tosti's.

examples.tl: Een tosti ham-kaas, alstublieft.
examples.en: A ham and cheese toastie, please.

notes.notes: Deep-fried ragout roll, from a snack-bar wall (FEBO) or as 'broodje kroket' with mustard. Plural: kroketten.

examples.tl: Twee broodjes kroket met mosterd, graag.
examples.en: Two croquette sandwiches with mustard, please.

notes.notes: A café is a pub that also serves coffee and lunch. 'Bruin café' = old-style pub. A 'coffeeshop' sells cannabis, not coffee.

examples.tl: Zullen we naar het café op de hoek gaan?
examples.en: Shall we go to the bar on the corner?

notes.notes: The tables outside a café. Plural: terrassen. Sit down and a waiter comes, or order inside if nobody does.

examples.tl: Zullen we op het terras gaan zitten?
examples.en: Shall we sit outside on the terrace?

notes.notes: Albert Heijn (AH), Jumbo, Lidl. 'AH to go' at stations is the nearest thing to a convenience store. Plural: supermarkten.

examples.tl: Ik haal even water bij de supermarkt.
examples.en: I'll just get some water at the supermarket.

notes.notes: Expect the counter-question 'Heeft u gereserveerd?' (do you have a reservation?).

examples.tl: Goedenavond. Een tafel voor twee, alstublieft. — Heeft u gereserveerd?
examples.en: Good evening. A table for two, please. — Do you have a reservation?

notes.en: May I have the menu, please?
accept: Can I have the menu, please?
Could I see the menu, please?
notes.notes: Locals mostly say 'Mag ik de kaart?' Many places have a QR code instead.

examples.tl: Mag ik de menukaart, alstublieft? — Natuurlijk, alstublieft.
examples.en: May I have the menu, please? — Of course, here you are.

notes.notes: Waiters do not hover: catch their eye or raise a hand, then say this.

examples.tl: Pardon, we willen graag bestellen.
examples.en: Excuse me, we'd like to order.

notes.notes: The -tje is how beer is ordered: you get a small draft lager. Two: 'twee biertjes' or 'twee bier'.

examples.tl: Een biertje en een witte wijn, alstublieft.
examples.en: A beer and a white wine, please.

notes.en: May I have the bill, please?
accept: Can I have the check, please?
Can I have the bill, please?
notes.notes: Or 'Mogen we afrekenen?' (can we pay?). In cafés you often just walk up and pay at the bar.

examples.tl: Mag ik de rekening, alstublieft? — Komt eraan.
examples.en: May I have the bill, please? — Coming right up.

notes.notes: Splitting is completely normal here ('going Dutch'). Locals settle up afterwards with the Tikkie app.

examples.tl: Kunnen we apart betalen? — Ja hoor, wat had u?
examples.en: Can we pay separately? — Sure, what did you have?

notes.en: May I have some tap water?
accept: Can I have some tap water?
Could I get some tap water?
notes.notes: Kraan = tap. Tap water is excellent but not automatic: some restaurants charge a little or push bottled water.

examples.tl: Mag ik wat kraanwater? — Natuurlijk, ik breng een karaf.
examples.en: May I have some tap water? — Of course, I'll bring a carafe.

notes.notes: Swap in: pinda's (peanuts), gluten, lactose, schaaldieren (shellfish), ei (egg).

examples.tl: Ik ben allergisch voor pinda's. Zit er pindasaus bij?
examples.en: I'm allergic to peanuts. Does it come with peanut sauce?

notes.notes: 'Geen' because you are negating a noun. 'Ik ben vegetariër' = I am a vegetarian.

examples.tl: Ik eet geen vlees, maar wel vis.
examples.en: I don't eat meat, but I do eat fish.

accept: Does it have meat in it?
notes.notes: 'Zit er ... in?' = does it contain ...? Zit er ei in? Zit er alcohol in?

examples.tl: Zit er vlees in de erwtensoep? — Ja, rookworst.
examples.en: Is there meat in the pea soup? — Yes, smoked sausage.

notes.notes: Heerlijk is a notch above lekker. Said 'HAYR-luk'.

examples.tl: Dank u wel, het was heerlijk.
examples.en: Thank you, it was delicious.

notes.notes: Said by waiters and by people at the table before starting. Reply 'dank u' or say it back.

examples.tl: Alstublieft, twee pannenkoeken. Eet smakelijk!
examples.en: Here you are, two pancakes. Enjoy your meal!

notes.notes: Aanraden = to recommend, separable. Good for beer lists and cheese counters.

examples.tl: We twijfelen nog. Wat raadt u aan?
examples.en: We can't decide yet. What do you recommend?

notes.notes: 'Nog een' = one more. Name the drink if it is not obvious: 'Nog een biertje.'

examples.tl: Nog een biertje, alstublieft.
examples.en: Another beer, please.

notes.notes: Book ahead for dinner on Friday and Saturday; popular places fill up.

examples.tl: Ik heb gereserveerd voor twee personen om zeven uur.
examples.en: I have a reservation for two at seven o'clock.

notes.notes: The waiter's question when clearing the plates. Answer: 'Ja, het was lekker.'

examples.tl: Heeft het gesmaakt? — Ja, heerlijk, dank u.
examples.en: Did you enjoy it? — Yes, delicious, thank you.

notes.notes: What staff say when it is your turn to order, literally 'just say it'.

examples.tl: Zegt u het maar. — Een koffie verkeerd, alstublieft.
examples.en: Go ahead. — A latte, please.

notes.notes: Asked at every counter and market stall after your first item.

examples.tl: Anders nog iets? — Nee, dank u.
examples.en: Anything else? — No, thank you.

notes.notes: The standard answer to 'Anders nog iets?' when you are done ordering.

examples.tl: Anders nog iets? — Nee, dat was het.
examples.en: Anything else? — No, that's all.

notes.notes: Kitchens often close around 9 or 10 pm, earlier than in the US or Asia.

examples.tl: Is de keuken nog open? — Ja, tot tien uur.
examples.en: Is the kitchen still open? — Yes, until ten.

notes.notes: 'Met' alone = with mayonnaise. 'Patatje oorlog' = mayo, peanut sauce and onions. 'Zonder' = plain.

examples.tl: Een patatje met en een kroket, alstublieft.
examples.en: Fries with mayo and a croquette, please.

notes.notes: Meenemen = to take along. Said after the order at coffee bars, bakeries and snack bars.

examples.tl: Een cappuccino om mee te nemen, alstublieft.
examples.en: A cappuccino to go, please.

notes.notes: Asked at bakeries, coffee bars and snack bars. Answer: 'Hier opeten' or 'Meenemen, graag'.

examples.tl: Hier opeten of meenemen? — Meenemen, graag.
examples.en: Eat in or take away? — Take away, please.

notes.notes: Or name the total you want to pay: 'Maak er maar twintig van' (make it twenty).

examples.tl: Dat is negentien euro. — Hier is twintig, laat maar zitten.
examples.en: That's nineteen euros. — Here's twenty, keep the change.

notes.notes: Plural: treinen. Intercity = fast, Sprinter = stops everywhere. Plan with the NS app or 9292.

examples.tl: De trein naar Utrecht vertrekt van spoor vijf.
examples.en: The train to Utrecht leaves from platform five.

notes.notes: Said 'sta-SHON'. Plural: stations. Amsterdam Centraal is usually just 'Centraal' or 'CS'.

examples.tl: Het hotel ligt vlak bij het station.
examples.en: The hotel is right by the station.

notes.notes: The physical platform you stand on. The number on the boards is the 'spoor' (track). Plural: perrons.

examples.tl: We wachten op het perron.
examples.en: We're waiting on the platform.

notes.notes: Plural: kaartjes. For trains, trams, museums and concerts alike. 'Ticket' is understood too.

examples.tl: Waar kan ik een kaartje kopen?
examples.en: Where can I buy a ticket?

notes.notes: Informal: 'een enkeltje'. Ticket machines also have an English button.

examples.tl: Een enkele reis naar Haarlem, alstublieft.
examples.en: A one-way ticket to Haarlem, please.

notes.notes: Said 'ruh-TOOR'. Informal: 'een retourtje'. A 'dagretour' is a same-day return.

examples.tl: Een retour naar Den Haag, tweede klas, alstublieft.
examples.en: A return ticket to The Hague, second class, please.

notes.notes: OV = openbaar vervoer. Being replaced by OVpay: visitors just tap the same contactless bank card or phone in and out.

examples.tl: Kan ik hier een OV-chipkaart kopen?
examples.en: Can I buy a public transport card here?

notes.notes: Hold your card to the reader at the gate or in the tram until it beeps. Separable: ik check in. Also for hotels and flights.

examples.tl: U moet inchecken voordat u instapt.
examples.en: You have to check in before you board.

examples.tl: Ik check in met mijn telefoon.
examples.en: I check in with my phone.

notes.notes: Tap out with the SAME card or device when you leave, or you are charged a fixed correction fee. Separable: ik check uit.

examples.tl: Ik ben vergeten uit te checken. Wat moet ik doen?
examples.en: I forgot to check out. What should I do?

notes.notes: Separable: ik stap over. Also for trams and buses. In the NS app an 'overstap' is a transfer.

examples.tl: U moet in Utrecht overstappen.
examples.en: You have to change in Utrecht.

notes.notes: Shown on departure boards as '+5' (minutes). Plural: vertragingen.

examples.tl: De intercity naar Rotterdam heeft tien minuten vertraging.
examples.en: The intercity to Rotterdam is ten minutes late.

notes.notes: Said 'trem'. Plural: trams. You check in AND out on board, at the doors. Trams nearly always have right of way.

examples.tl: Tram twee rijdt langs het Rijksmuseum en het Vondelpark.
examples.en: Tram two runs past the Rijksmuseum and the Vondelpark.

notes.notes: Plural: bussen. Short rounded u, not 'boos'. No cash on board: card only.

examples.tl: De bus naar de Zaanse Schans vertrekt achter het station.
examples.en: The bus to Zaanse Schans leaves from behind the station.

notes.notes: Amsterdam and Rotterdam have one. Line 52 (Noord/Zuidlijn) links Amsterdam Centraal with station Zuid. Plural: metro's.

examples.tl: Neem de metro naar station Zuid.
examples.en: Take the metro to Zuid station.

notes.notes: Plural: haltes. 'Volgende halte' = next stop, on the screen and in the announcement.

examples.tl: Bij welke halte moet ik uitstappen?
examples.en: At which stop do I have to get off?

notes.notes: Plural: vliegvelden. 'Luchthaven' is the formal word. Schiphol is said 'SKHIP-hol'; its train station is under the terminal.

examples.tl: De trein naar het vliegveld rijdt elke tien minuten.
examples.en: The train to the airport runs every ten minutes.

notes.notes: Plural: vluchten. Short u plus the throaty ch: 'vlukht'.

examples.tl: Mijn vlucht naar Manila vertrekt om negen uur.
examples.en: My flight to Manila leaves at nine o'clock.

notes.notes: Plural: taxi's. Pricey. Found at ranks ('taxistandplaats') or by app, rarely hailed on the street.

examples.tl: Kunnen we een taxi nemen naar het hotel?
examples.en: Can we take a taxi to the hotel?

notes.notes: Said 'feets'. Plural: fietsen. 'Op de fiets' = by bike. Many rental bikes brake by pedalling backwards.

examples.tl: Bijna iedereen gaat hier op de fiets.
examples.en: Almost everyone here goes by bike.

notes.notes: Plural: fietspaden. Usually red asphalt. Never stand or walk on it: cyclists are fast and ring rather than brake.

examples.tl: Blijf op de stoep, dit is het fietspad.
examples.en: Stay on the sidewalk, this is the bike path.

notes.notes: Ik huur. 'Te huur' = for rent. Fietsverhuur = bike rental; expect to leave ID or a deposit ('borg').

examples.tl: We willen twee fietsen huren voor één dag.
examples.en: We'd like to rent two bikes for one day.

notes.notes: Ik vertrek, de trein vertrekt; past: vertrokken. Opposite: aankomen (to arrive).

examples.tl: De bus vertrekt over vijf minuten.
examples.en: The bus leaves in five minutes.

notes.notes: Separable: ik stap uit. Opposite: instappen (to get on). Press the stop button in trams and buses.

examples.tl: We stappen bij de volgende halte uit.
examples.en: We're getting off at the next stop.

notes.notes: In NS announcements: 'door een storing' = because of a fault. Plural: storingen. The NS app shows alternatives.

examples.tl: Door een storing rijden er geen treinen naar Schiphol.
examples.en: Because of a disruption no trains are running to Schiphol.

notes.notes: Naar = to (a destination). At a counter or machine; if you tap in with a bank card you need no ticket at all.

examples.tl: Eén kaartje naar Utrecht, alstublieft. — Enkele reis of retour?
examples.en: One ticket to Utrecht, please. — One way or return?

notes.tl: Van welk spoor vertrekt de trein naar Schiphol?
notes.en: Which platform does the Schiphol train leave from?
accept: Which platform does the train to Schiphol leave from?
What platform is the train to Schiphol?
notes.notes: 'Welk' because spoor is a het-word. Platforms change at short notice: check the board again.

examples.tl: Van welk spoor vertrekt de trein naar Schiphol? — Van spoor veertien.
examples.en: Which platform does the train to Schiphol leave from? — From platform fourteen.

notes.tl: Hoe laat vertrekt de volgende trein?
notes.en: What time does the next train leave?
accept: When does the next train leave?
What time is the next train?
notes.notes: Volgende = next. Most main routes run every 10 to 30 minutes.

examples.tl: Hoe laat vertrekt de volgende trein naar Den Haag?
examples.en: What time does the next train to The Hague leave?

accept: Do I have to change trains?
notes.notes: 'Rechtstreeks' = direct, no change.

examples.tl: Moet ik overstappen? — Nee, deze trein rijdt rechtstreeks.
examples.en: Do I have to change? — No, this train is direct.

notes.en: Does this train stop in Leiden?
notes.notes: Intercity trains skip small stations: check the screen on the platform.

examples.tl: Stopt deze trein ook in Delft?
examples.en: Does this train also stop in Delft?

notes.notes: No seat reservations on domestic trains: sit anywhere in your class (1 or 2 is marked by the door).

examples.tl: Is deze plaats vrij? — Ja hoor, ga zitten.
examples.en: Is this seat free? — Sure, sit down.

notes.tl: Kan ik met mijn bankpas inchecken?
notes.en: Can I check in with my bank card?
accept: Can I tap in with my bank card?
notes.notes: Yes: OVpay takes contactless debit and credit cards and phones on trains, trams, buses and metro.

examples.tl: Kan ik met mijn creditcard inchecken in de tram?
examples.en: Can I check in with my credit card on the tram?

accept: Do not forget to check out.
notes.notes: Heard in announcements and shown on screens in trams and buses.

examples.tl: Vergeet niet uit te checken als u uitstapt.
examples.en: Don't forget to check out when you get off.

notes.tl: Waar kan ik een fiets huren?
notes.en: Where can I rent a bike?
accept: Where can I hire a bike?
notes.notes: Rental shops cluster around Centraal Station. Ask for 'handremmen' if you want hand brakes.

examples.tl: Waar kan ik een fiets huren? — Bij de fietsenwinkel om de hoek.
examples.en: Where can I rent a bike? — At the bike shop around the corner.

notes.notes: Shouted, with a bike bell, when you step onto a bike path. Move aside first, apologize after.

examples.tl: Kijk uit, een fiets!
examples.en: Watch out, a bike!

notes.en: You're walking on the bike path.
accept: You are walking on the bike path.
You're walking in the bike lane.
notes.notes: What a cyclist tells a tourist, rarely this politely. The 'stoep' (sidewalk) is for walking.

examples.tl: Pardon, u loopt op het fietspad. De stoep is daar.
examples.en: Excuse me, you're walking on the bike path. The sidewalk is over there.

notes.tl: Welke tram gaat naar het Museumplein?
accept: Which tram goes to the Museumplein?
notes.notes: 'Welke' with de-words (tram, bus, trein), 'welk' with het-words (spoor, perron).

examples.tl: Welke tram gaat naar het Museumplein? — Tram twee of twaalf.
examples.en: Which tram goes to Museumplein? — Tram two or twelve.

notes.notes: For a taxi driver. Give an address the same way: 'Naar de Prinsengracht 12, alstublieft.'

examples.tl: Goedemorgen. Naar Schiphol, alstublieft.
examples.en: Good morning. To Schiphol, please.

notes.tl: Hoeveel kost een rit naar het centrum?
notes.en: How much is a ride to the center?
accept: How much does a ride to the center cost?
How much is a ride to the centre?
notes.notes: Rit = ride. Taxis run on the meter; ask for a rough price before you get in.

examples.tl: Hoeveel kost een rit naar het centrum, ongeveer?
examples.en: Roughly how much is a ride to the center?

notes.notes: Dutch trains 'have' a delay. 'Rijdt niet' on the board means cancelled.

examples.tl: De trein heeft twintig minuten vertraging, dus ik ben wat later.
examples.en: The train is twenty minutes late, so I'll be a bit later.

notes.notes: Balie = desk, counter. Schiphol is one terminal with departure halls ('vertrekhal') 1, 2 and 3.

examples.tl: Waar is de incheckbalie van KLM?
examples.en: Where is the KLM check-in desk?

notes.tl: Waar kan ik mijn bagage ophalen?
notes.en: Where can I pick up my luggage?
accept: Where can I collect my luggage?
Where can I get my baggage?
notes.notes: Ophalen = to pick up, collect. The belt is the 'bagageband'.

examples.tl: Waar kan ik mijn bagage ophalen? — Bij band zes.
examples.en: Where can I pick up my luggage? — At belt six.

notes.notes: Aansluiting = connection. Missed your train? 'Ik heb mijn trein gemist.' Regular tickets are valid on the next one.

examples.tl: Ik heb mijn aansluiting gemist door de vertraging.
examples.en: I missed my connection because of the delay.

accept: This train does not go any further.
notes.notes: A standard NS announcement: everyone off. Listen for 'eindpunt' (final stop) too.

examples.tl: Dames en heren, deze trein rijdt niet verder dan Leiden.
examples.en: Ladies and gentlemen, this train goes no further than Leiden.

notes.tl: Is dit de trein naar Rotterdam?
notes.en: Is this the train to Rotterdam?
notes.notes: Swap in 'de tram' or 'de bus'. Some trains split on the way: check you are in the right half.

examples.tl: Pardon, is dit de trein naar Rotterdam Centraal?
examples.en: Excuse me, is this the train to Rotterdam Centraal?

notes.notes: For squeezing out of a full tram. On escalators people stand right and walk left.

examples.tl: Pardon, mag ik er even langs? Ik moet hier uitstappen.
examples.en: Excuse me, may I get past? I have to get off here.

notes.notes: 'Waar is...?' = where is...? 'Waar ... naartoe?' = where to? Also means 'true'.

examples.tl: Waar is de ingang?
examples.en: Where is the entrance?

examples.tl: Waar gaat deze bus naartoe?
examples.en: Where does this bus go?

notes.notes: 'Linksaf' = (turn) left. 'Aan de linkerkant' = on the left-hand side.

examples.tl: Het museum is links, na de brug.
examples.en: The museum is on the left, after the bridge.

notes.notes: 'Rechtsaf' = (turn) right. Traffic from the right usually has priority, bikes included.

examples.tl: De ingang is rechts van de kerk.
examples.en: The entrance is to the right of the church.

notes.notes: Not to be confused with 'rechts' (right). 'Steeds rechtdoor' = keep going straight.

examples.tl: Ga rechtdoor tot aan de gracht.
examples.en: Go straight ahead as far as the canal.

notes.notes: 'Is het dichtbij?' Before a place it is two words: 'dicht bij het station'. 'Vlakbij' = very close.

examples.tl: Het hotel is heel dichtbij, twee minuten lopen.
examples.en: The hotel is very close, a two-minute walk.

notes.notes: 'Hoe ver?' = how far? 'Niet ver' = not far. Verder = further.

examples.tl: Het strand is te ver om te lopen.
examples.en: The beach is too far to walk.

notes.notes: Plural: kaarten. Also 'card' and 'menu'. A street map of a town is a 'plattegrond'.

examples.tl: Heeft u een kaart van de stad?
examples.en: Do you have a map of the city?

notes.notes: Plural: straten. In addresses the number follows the name: Damstraat 12.

examples.tl: In welke straat is het hotel?
examples.en: Which street is the hotel on?

notes.notes: A city canal lined with houses: Prinsengracht, Herengracht. Plural: grachten. Two throaty sounds: 'khrakht'.

examples.tl: Ons hotel ligt aan de Keizersgracht.
examples.en: Our hotel is on the Keizersgracht.

notes.notes: Plural: bruggen. Many bridges open for boats: wait behind the barrier.

examples.tl: Ga de brug over en dan links.
examples.en: Cross the bridge and then go left.

notes.notes: Said 'playn'. Plural: pleinen. Museumplein, Leidseplein, Rembrandtplein; the main one is just 'de Dam'.

examples.tl: We spreken af op het plein voor het station.
examples.en: We're meeting on the square in front of the station.

notes.notes: Said 'hook'. Plural: hoeken. 'Op de hoek' = on the corner.

examples.tl: Er is een bakker op de hoek.
examples.en: There's a bakery on the corner.

notes.notes: Plural: stoplichten. Bikes have their own small lights: check those too before you cross.

examples.tl: Bij het stoplicht gaat u linksaf.
examples.en: At the traffic light you turn left.

notes.notes: Signs just say 'Centrum'. Plural: centra.

examples.tl: Het centrum is tien minuten lopen vanaf hier.
examples.en: The center is a ten-minute walk from here.

notes.notes: Stress on the last part: tay-khun-OH-ver.

examples.tl: De halte is tegenover de supermarkt.
examples.en: The stop is opposite the supermarket.

notes.notes: Related: achter (behind), voor (in front of), tussen (between).

examples.tl: De apotheek zit naast de Albert Heijn.
examples.en: The pharmacy is next to the Albert Heijn.

notes.notes: Separable: ik steek over. Look both ways twice: bikes and trams come from both directions.

examples.tl: U moet hier oversteken, bij het zebrapad.
examples.en: You need to cross here, at the crosswalk.

notes.notes: Public toilets are scarce and often paid (also in stations). Cafés expect you to buy something first.

examples.tl: Pardon, waar is het toilet? — Achterin, de trap af.
examples.en: Excuse me, where is the toilet? — At the back, down the stairs.

notes.notes: For two or more: 'We zijn verdwaald.'

examples.tl: Ik ben verdwaald. Kunt u mij helpen?
examples.en: I'm lost. Can you help me?

notes.tl: Hoe kom ik bij het Rijksmuseum?
notes.en: How do I get to the Rijksmuseum?
notes.notes: Pattern: Hoe kom ik bij + building or place? For an area: 'Hoe kom ik in het centrum?'

examples.tl: Hoe kom ik bij het Rijksmuseum? — Met tram twee, of lopend.
examples.en: How do I get to the Rijksmuseum? — By tram two, or on foot.

notes.notes: Answers come in minutes: 'een kwartier lopen' = a fifteen-minute walk.

examples.tl: Is het ver? — Nee, een kwartier lopen.
examples.en: Is it far? — No, a fifteen-minute walk.

notes.notes: Distances are given in minutes 'lopen' (walking) or 'fietsen' (cycling).

examples.tl: Het is vijf minuten lopen vanaf het station.
examples.en: It's a five-minute walk from the station.

notes.tl: Kunt u het op de kaart aanwijzen?
notes.en: Can you show me on the map?
accept: Could you point it out on the map?
Can you show it on the map?
notes.notes: Aanwijzen = to point out. Works just as well with your phone held out.

examples.tl: Ik zoek deze straat. Kunt u het op de kaart aanwijzen?
examples.en: I'm looking for this street. Can you show me on the map?

notes.en: The first street on the left.
notes.notes: Eerste = first, tweede = second, derde = third.

examples.tl: Neem de eerste straat links en dan de tweede rechts.
examples.en: Take the first street on the left and then the second on the right.

notes.en: Turn right at the traffic light.
notes.notes: Directions usually drop the verb. Linksaf = turn left, rechtsaf = turn right.

examples.tl: Bij het stoplicht rechtsaf en dan steeds rechtdoor.
examples.en: Right at the traffic light and then keep going straight.

notes.notes: 'Ik zoek ...' = I'm looking for ...: ik zoek het station, ik zoek een pinautomaat.

examples.tl: Ik zoek dit adres. Weet u waar het is?
examples.en: I'm looking for this address. Do you know where it is?

notes.tl: Is dit de weg naar het centrum?
notes.en: Is this the way to the center?
accept: Is this the way to the centre?
notes.notes: Weg = way, road. 'Gewoon rechtdoor' = just straight on.

examples.tl: Pardon, is dit de weg naar het centrum? — Ja, gewoon rechtdoor.
examples.en: Excuse me, is this the way to the center? — Yes, just straight on.

notes.tl: Is er een supermarkt in de buurt?
accept: Is there a supermarket around here?
Is there a supermarket near here?
notes.notes: 'In de buurt' = in the neighbourhood. Swap in any place: een apotheek, een pinautomaat, een toilet.

examples.tl: Is er een pinautomaat in de buurt?
examples.en: Is there an ATM nearby?

notes.notes: 'Hier om de hoek' = just around the corner from here.

examples.tl: De bakker zit hier om de hoek.
examples.en: The bakery is just around the corner.

notes.notes: Kant = side, direction. Answer: 'die kant op' (that way), with a pointed finger.

examples.tl: Welke kant op? — Die kant op, richting de Dam.
examples.en: Which way? — That way, toward Dam Square.

notes.notes: Said 'khelt'. No plural. Contant geld = cash; kleingeld = small change.

examples.tl: Ik heb niet genoeg geld bij me.
examples.en: I don't have enough money on me.

notes.notes: Said 'UH-ro' (eu as in French 'peu'). Singular after numbers: vijf euro. € 3,50 is said 'drie vijftig' or 'drie euro vijftig'.

examples.tl: Dat is dan twaalf euro vijftig.
examples.en: That comes to twelve euros fifty.

notes.notes: Said 'prays'. Plural: prijzen. Shelf prices already include tax (btw). Also means 'prize'.

examples.tl: De prijs staat op het kaartje.
examples.en: The price is on the tag.

notes.notes: 'Te duur' = too expensive; duurder = more expensive.

examples.tl: Amsterdam is behoorlijk duur.
examples.en: Amsterdam is pretty expensive.

notes.notes: Said 'khoot-KOHP'. Goedkoper = cheaper.

examples.tl: Heeft u iets goedkopers?
examples.en: Do you have something cheaper?

notes.notes: Ik betaal; past: betaald. Afrekenen = to settle up, pay the bill.

examples.tl: Waar kan ik betalen?
examples.en: Where can I pay?

notes.notes: Cash totals are rounded to the nearest 5 cents: 1 and 2 cent coins are not used.

examples.tl: Ik betaal liever contant.
examples.en: I'd rather pay in cash.

notes.notes: Said as in English. Visa and Mastercard work in most places now, but some small shops and stalls take debit cards only.

examples.tl: Accepteert u creditcards?
examples.en: Do you accept credit cards?

notes.notes: Plural: pinpassen. What locals pay with, contactless, even for one coffee.

examples.tl: Ik ben mijn pinpas vergeten.
examples.en: I forgot my debit card.

notes.notes: Also 'pinautomaat'. The banks' shared ATMs are yellow and branded 'Geldmaat'. Plural: geldautomaten.

examples.tl: De geldautomaat staat naast de supermarkt.
examples.en: The ATM is next to the supermarket.

notes.notes: Often 'bonnetje'. Plural: bonnen. Keep it for exchanges and tax-free forms.

examples.tl: Mag ik de bon, alstublieft?
examples.en: May I have the receipt, please?

notes.notes: Plural: winkels. Winkelen = to go shopping. Most shops close at 6 pm, supermarkets later.

examples.tl: De winkels gaan om tien uur open.
examples.en: The shops open at ten o'clock.

notes.notes: Plural: markten. The Albert Cuypmarkt in Amsterdam runs Monday to Saturday.

examples.tl: Op de markt is de kaas goedkoper.
examples.en: Cheese is cheaper at the market.

notes.notes: Ik koop; past: gekocht. Opposite: verkopen (to sell).

examples.tl: Waar kan ik een simkaart kopen?
examples.en: Where can I buy a SIM card?

notes.notes: Plural: maten. EU sizes: a US men's shoe 10 is about 43-44. S / M / L are used too.

examples.tl: Welke maat heeft u?
examples.en: What size are you?

notes.notes: Plural: tassen. A shopping bag is a 'tasje' and costs a few cents. Rugzak = backpack.

examples.tl: Ik heb mijn eigen tas bij me.
examples.en: I have my own bag with me.

notes.notes: Plural: kortingen. '50% korting' on shop windows. Uitverkoop = clearance sale; aanbieding = special offer.

examples.tl: Krijg ik korting als ik er twee koop?
examples.en: Do I get a discount if I buy two?

notes.notes: Plural: kassa's. Also the ticket desk in a museum. Zelfscankassa = self-checkout.

examples.tl: U kunt bij de kassa betalen.
examples.en: You can pay at the checkout.

notes.notes: The spoken word; signs say 'geopend'. 'Open gaan' = to open (of shops).

examples.tl: Is de supermarkt op zondag open?
examples.en: Is the supermarket open on Sunday?

notes.notes: The spoken word; signs say 'gesloten'. 'Dicht gaan' = to close (of shops).

examples.tl: De bakker is op maandag dicht.
examples.en: The bakery is closed on Mondays.

notes.notes: A deposit of 15 cents on cans and small plastic bottles, 25 on large ones. Supermarket return machines give a refund slip.

examples.tl: Op dit flesje zit statiegeld.
examples.en: There's a deposit on this bottle.

notes.notes: Hoeveel = how much / how many. Equally common: 'Wat kost dit?'

examples.tl: Hoeveel kost dit? — Zeven euro vijftig.
examples.en: How much is this? — Seven euros fifty.

notes.en: Can I pay by credit card?
accept: Can I pay with a credit card?
notes.notes: Worth asking in small shops, at markets and in brown cafés before you order.

examples.tl: Kan ik met creditcard betalen? — Ja hoor, dat kan.
examples.en: Can I pay by credit card? — Sure, you can.

notes.notes: Not a given: plenty of cafés and shops, and all buses, are card-only ('alleen pinnen').

examples.tl: Kan ik contant betalen? — Nee, helaas, alleen met pin.
examples.en: Can I pay cash? — No, sorry, card only.

notes.notes: The answer to 'Kan ik u helpen?' in a shop. Staff will then leave you alone.

examples.tl: Kan ik u helpen? — Nee, dank u, ik kijk alleen even.
examples.en: Can I help you? — No, thank you, I'm just looking.

notes.tl: Heeft u dit in een andere maat?
notes.en: Do you have this in another size?
accept: Do you have this in a different size?
notes.notes: Groter = bigger, kleiner = smaller. 'In een andere kleur' = in another colour.

examples.tl: Heeft u dit in een maat groter?
examples.en: Do you have this one size bigger?

notes.notes: Passen = to try on (and to fit). Paskamer = fitting room.

examples.tl: Mag ik dit passen? — Ja, de paskamers zijn achterin.
examples.en: May I try this on? — Yes, the fitting rooms are at the back.

notes.notes: Present tense does the job of English 'I'll'. 'Deze' = this one (de-word), 'dit' for a het-word.

examples.tl: Ik neem deze. Kan ik pinnen?
examples.en: I'll take this one. Can I pay by card?

notes.notes: 'Te' + adjective = too: te groot (too big), te klein (too small).

examples.tl: Het is mooi, maar het is te duur voor mij.
examples.en: It's nice, but it's too expensive for me.

notes.notes: Asked at almost every till, often shortened to 'Bonnetje?' or 'Bonnetje erbij?'

examples.tl: Wilt u de bon? — Ja, graag.
examples.en: Do you want the receipt? — Yes, please.

notes.notes: Shops may not give plastic bags away free, so you are always asked.

examples.tl: Wilt u een tasje? — Nee, dank u, ik heb een tas.
examples.en: Would you like a bag? — No, thank you, I have a bag.

accept: Where can I take out money?
notes.notes: Geld opnemen = to withdraw money. ATMs are thinner on the ground than they used to be.

examples.tl: Waar kan ik geld opnemen? — Er is een geldautomaat bij het station.
examples.en: Where can I withdraw money? — There's an ATM at the station.

notes.notes: Ruilen = swap for another item. 'Geld terug' (money back) is not always offered. Bring the receipt.

examples.tl: Kan ik dit ruilen? Het is te klein.
examples.en: Can I exchange this? It's too small.

notes.en: Can I get the VAT back?
accept: Can I get a tax refund?
Can I get the tax back?
notes.notes: btw (said 'bay-tay-way') = VAT, 21%. Non-EU residents can reclaim it on larger purchases: ask for a tax-free form, show your passport.

examples.tl: Ik woon buiten de EU. Kan ik de btw terugkrijgen?
examples.en: I live outside the EU. Can I get the VAT back?

notes.tl: Tot hoe laat bent u open?
notes.en: Until what time are you open?
accept_tl: Tot hoe laat zijn jullie open?
notes.notes: 'Tot' = until. To a young shop assistant: 'Tot hoe laat zijn jullie open?'

examples.tl: Tot hoe laat bent u open? — Tot zes uur.
examples.en: Until what time are you open? — Until six.

notes.tl: Kan er nog iets van de prijs af?
notes.en: Can you go down on the price?
accept: Can you do a better price?
Can you give me a discount?
accept_tl: Kan er nog wat van de prijs af?
notes.notes: Only at flea markets (Waterlooplein, IJ-Hallen) and for second-hand things. Haggling in shops is not done.

examples.tl: Twintig euro is wel veel. Kan er nog iets van de prijs af?
examples.en: Twenty euros is a lot. Can you go down on the price?

notes.notes: Stress on the second syllable: ho-TEL. Plural: hotels. Tourist tax ('toeristenbelasting') often comes on top of the price.

examples.tl: Het hotel ligt aan een gracht.
examples.en: The hotel is on a canal.

notes.notes: Plural: kamers. Eenpersoonskamer = single, tweepersoonskamer = double.

examples.tl: Ik heb een kamer voor drie nachten geboekt.
examples.en: I've booked a room for three nights.

notes.notes: Said 'SLUH-tul' (eu as in French 'peu'). Plural: sleutels. A key card is a 'sleutelkaart' or 'pasje'.

examples.tl: Mag ik de sleutel van kamer twaalf?
examples.en: May I have the key to room twelve?

notes.notes: Plural: reserveringen. Reserveren = to reserve.

examples.tl: De reservering is voor twee nachten.
examples.en: The reservation is for two nights.

notes.notes: Said 'ba-KHA-zhuh', the second g as in French. No plural.

examples.tl: Mijn bagage is nog niet aangekomen.
examples.en: My luggage hasn't arrived yet.

notes.notes: Plural: koffers. Old canal houses have very steep stairs and often no lift: pack light.

examples.tl: Mijn koffer is te zwaar voor de trap.
examples.en: My suitcase is too heavy for the stairs.

notes.notes: Plural: paspoorten. Hotels ask for it at check-in, and you are required to be able to show ID in the Netherlands.

examples.tl: Mag ik uw paspoort even zien?
examples.en: May I see your passport for a moment?

notes.notes: Begane grond (BG) = ground floor; eerste verdieping = one flight up, the US second floor.

examples.tl: Uw kamer is op de derde verdieping.
examples.en: Your room is on the third floor.

notes.notes: Plural: liften. Not a given in old buildings: ask before booking a top-floor room.

examples.tl: Is er een lift in het hotel?
examples.en: Is there an elevator in the hotel?

notes.notes: Said 'ont-BAYT'. Typically bread, cheese, cold cuts, a boiled egg and hagelslag (chocolate sprinkles).

examples.tl: Het ontbijt is van zeven tot tien uur.
examples.en: Breakfast is from seven to ten.

notes.notes: Said 'HAN-dook'. Plural: handdoeken.

examples.tl: Er liggen geen handdoeken in de badkamer.
examples.en: There are no towels in the bathroom.

notes.notes: Said 'doosh', as in French. Plural: douches. Badkamer = bathroom, bad = bathtub.

examples.tl: Heeft de kamer een eigen douche?
examples.en: Does the room have its own shower?

notes.notes: Air conditioning ('airco') is rare outside newer hotels.

examples.tl: Hoe zet ik de verwarming aan?
examples.en: How do I turn on the heating?

notes.notes: Said 'WEE-fee' in Dutch. Free on NS trains and in most cafés.

examples.tl: Is er gratis wifi op de kamer?
examples.en: Is there free Wi-Fi in the room?

notes.notes: Plural: wachtwoorden. Hoofdletter = capital letter, cijfer = digit.

examples.tl: Het wachtwoord staat op het kaartje bij de sleutel.
examples.en: The password is on the card with the key.

notes.notes: Plural: nachten. 'Per nacht' = per night. The evening before bedtime is 'avond'.

examples.tl: Hoeveel kost de kamer per nacht?
examples.en: How much is the room per night?

notes.notes: Plural: stopcontacten. Round two-pin European type, 230 V: US plugs need an adapter ('verloopstekker').

examples.tl: Is er een stopcontact bij het bed?
examples.en: Is there an outlet by the bed?

notes.notes: For hotel and restaurant bookings. Be ready to spell: 'Zal ik het spellen?' = shall I spell it?

examples.tl: Ik heb een reservering op naam van Miller.
examples.en: I have a reservation under the name Miller.

accept: I would like to check in.
notes.notes: Check-in is usually from 3 pm. If you are early, ask to leave your bags.

examples.tl: Goedemiddag, ik wil graag inchecken. Ik heb een reservering.
examples.en: Good afternoon, I'd like to check in. I have a reservation.

accept: What time do I have to check out?
When do I have to check out?
notes.notes: Usually 10 or 11 am. 'Kan ik later uitchecken?' = can I check out later?

examples.tl: Hoe laat moet ik uitchecken? — Voor elf uur.
examples.en: What time do I have to check out? — Before eleven.

accept_tl: Is het ontbijt bij de prijs inbegrepen?
notes.notes: Inbegrepen = included; booking sites write 'inclusief ontbijt' or 'exclusief ontbijt'.

examples.tl: Is het ontbijt inbegrepen? — Nee, dat is vijftien euro per persoon.
examples.en: Is breakfast included? — No, that's fifteen euros per person.

notes.tl: Wat is het wachtwoord van de wifi?
notes.notes: Works in cafés too, where it is often written on the receipt or the menu.

examples.tl: Wat is het wachtwoord van de wifi? — Dat staat op uw sleutelkaart.
examples.en: What is the Wi-Fi password? — It's on your key card.

notes.tl: Kan ik mijn bagage hier laten?
notes.en: Can I leave my luggage here?
accept: May I leave my luggage here?
Can I leave my bags here?
accept_tl: Kan ik mijn bagage hier achterlaten?
Mag ik mijn bagage hier laten?
notes.notes: Hotels usually store bags free before check-in and after check-out. Big stations have lockers ('bagagekluizen').

examples.tl: Kan ik mijn bagage hier laten tot vanmiddag?
examples.en: Can I leave my luggage here until this afternoon?

notes.notes: '... doet het niet' = ... is not working. Fits anything: de wifi, de verwarming, de lift, de tv.

examples.tl: De verwarming doet het niet. Kunt u iemand sturen?
examples.en: The heating isn't working. Can you send someone?

notes.notes: 'Er is geen ...' = there is no ...: er is geen zeep (soap), geen wc-papier (toilet paper).

examples.tl: Er is geen warm water in kamer acht.
examples.en: There's no hot water in room eight.

accept: Could I have one more towel?
notes.notes: 'Nog een' = one more. Kussen = pillow, deken = blanket.

examples.tl: Mag ik nog een handdoek en een extra kussen?
examples.en: May I have another towel and an extra pillow?

notes.tl: Heeft u een kamer vrij voor vannacht?
notes.en: Do you have a room for tonight?
accept: Do you have a room free for tonight?
Do you have a room available tonight?
accept_tl: Heeft u nog een kamer vrij voor vannacht?
notes.notes: Vannacht = the coming night. 'Vol' or 'volgeboekt' = full. Amsterdam fills up on race and festival weekends.

examples.tl: Heeft u een kamer vrij voor vannacht? — Helaas, we zitten vol.
examples.en: Do you have a room for tonight? — Unfortunately we're full.

notes.tl: Kan ik een andere kamer krijgen?
notes.en: Can I get a different room?
notes.notes: Lawaaiig = noisy; 'aan de straatkant' = on the street side; 'aan de achterkant' = at the back.

examples.tl: Het is erg lawaaiig. Kan ik een andere kamer krijgen?
examples.en: It's very noisy. Can I get a different room?

notes.tl: Waar kan ik mijn was doen?
notes.en: Where can I do my laundry?
accept: Where can I wash my clothes?
notes.notes: 'De was' = the laundry. Wasserette = laundromat; wasmachine = washer, droger = dryer.

examples.tl: Waar kan ik mijn was doen? — Er is een wasserette om de hoek.
examples.en: Where can I do my laundry? — There's a laundromat around the corner.

notes.notes: 'Ik ben ... kwijt' = I have lost ...: it works for anything you can lose.

examples.tl: Sorry, ik ben mijn sleutel kwijt. Wat nu?
examples.en: Sorry, I've lost my key. What now?

notes.tl: Kunt u een taxi voor mij bellen?
notes.en: Can you call a taxi for me?
accept: Could you call me a taxi?
Can you call me a taxi?
notes.notes: Bellen = to phone. For an early flight, ask the evening before.

examples.tl: Kunt u een taxi voor mij bellen? Ik moet om zes uur naar Schiphol.
examples.en: Can you call a taxi for me? I have to leave for Schiphol at six.

notes.notes: On green signs in stations, shops and car parks. 'Uit' alone on a door also means exit. Plural: uitgangen.

examples.tl: De uitgang is aan de andere kant van het perron.
examples.en: The exit is at the other end of the platform.

notes.notes: On buildings, museums and car parks. Hoofdingang = main entrance. Plural: ingangen.

examples.tl: De ingang van het museum is om de hoek.
examples.en: The museum entrance is around the corner.

notes.notes: On shop and café doors. Said 'DUU-wun'.

examples.tl: Je moet duwen, niet trekken.
examples.en: You have to push, not pull.

notes.notes: On doors, the opposite of 'duwen'. Learn the two as a pair: they are easy to mix up.

examples.tl: Op de deur staat 'trekken'.
examples.en: The door says 'pull'.

notes.notes: On shop and museum doors: 'maandag gesloten' = closed on Mondays. In speech people say 'dicht'.

examples.tl: Het museum is vandaag gesloten.
examples.en: The museum is closed today.

notes.notes: On doors and opening-hours signs: 'geopend van 9.00 tot 17.00 uur'. In speech people say 'open'.

examples.tl: Dagelijks geopend van tien tot vijf.
examples.en: Open daily from ten to five.

notes.notes: At stations, on platforms and in every bar and restaurant. Rookvrij = smoke-free. Verboden = forbidden.

examples.tl: Op het hele station is het verboden te roken.
examples.en: Smoking is forbidden throughout the station.

notes.notes: On toilet doors, often just 'H', or 'M' for mannen. Singular: heer.

examples.tl: De deur met 'heren' is het herentoilet.
examples.en: The door marked 'heren' is the men's toilet.

notes.notes: On toilet doors, often just 'D', or 'V' for vrouwen. Singular: dame.

examples.tl: Links staat 'dames', rechts 'heren'.
examples.en: It says 'ladies' on the left, 'men' on the right.

notes.notes: Said 'twa-LET'. Signs say 'toiletten' or 'WC' (said 'way-say'). Station toilets are usually paid, by card.

examples.tl: Het toilet is alleen voor klanten.
examples.en: The toilet is for customers only.

notes.notes: The platform number on station boards: 'spoor 5a' (a / b = which end). The platform itself is 'perron'. Plural: sporen.

examples.tl: De trein naar Schiphol vertrekt van spoor veertien.
examples.en: The train to Schiphol leaves from platform fourteen.

notes.notes: On warning signs and station screens: 'Let op! Zakkenrollers' (pickpockets), 'Let op: gewijzigd vertrekspoor' (platform change).

examples.tl: Let op: deze deur sluit automatisch.
examples.en: Attention: this door closes automatically.

notes.notes: On ticket sites, concert posters and empty bakery shelves. Not the same as 'uitverkoop' (clearance sale).

examples.tl: De kaartjes voor vanavond zijn uitverkocht.
examples.en: The tickets for tonight are sold out.

notes.notes: On tills, café doors, market stalls and buses. Also 'geen contant geld' or 'pin only'. Alleen = only.

examples.tl: Bij deze kassa kunt u alleen pinnen.
examples.en: At this checkout you can pay by card only.

notes.notes: On the yellow timetable posters in stations and on Schiphol signs. Vertrektijd = departure time.

examples.tl: Kijk op het bord onder 'vertrek' voor het juiste spoor.
examples.en: Check the board under 'departures' for the right platform.

notes.notes: At Schiphol 'Aankomst' marks the arrivals halls. Also on timetables next to 'vertrek'.

examples.tl: We wachten op je bij 'aankomst 2' op Schiphol.
examples.en: We'll wait for you at 'arrivals 2' at Schiphol.

notes.notes: On green signs in buildings, trains and trams. Nood = emergency (noodrem = emergency brake).

examples.tl: Houd de nooduitgang vrij.
examples.en: Keep the emergency exit clear.

notes.notes: On gates, building sites and staff doors. Also 'geen toegang'.

examples.tl: Op het hek staat 'verboden toegang'.
examples.en: The gate says 'no entry'.

notes.notes: On toilet locks (red) and lockers. 'Is deze stoel bezet?' = is this seat taken?

examples.tl: Alle kluisjes zijn bezet.
examples.en: All the lockers are occupied.

notes.notes: On toilet locks (green), taxis and car-park displays: free = not taken. Free of charge is 'gratis'.

examples.tl: Bij de parkeergarage staat: 120 plaatsen vrij.
examples.en: The car park sign says: 120 spaces free.

notes.notes: Said 'KHRAH-tis'. On signs for wifi, entry and samples. The ferries behind Amsterdam Centraal are gratis.

examples.tl: De pont naar Amsterdam-Noord is gratis.
examples.en: The ferry to Amsterdam-Noord is free.

notes.notes: Taped to ticket machines, lifts and escalators. Also 'buiten gebruik' or 'buiten dienst' (out of service).

examples.tl: De kaartautomaat is defect.
examples.en: The ticket machine is out of order.

notes.notes: On bike-rental shops, boats and apartments. 'Te koop' = for sale.

examples.tl: Fietsen te huur vanaf twaalf euro per dag.
examples.en: Bikes for rent from twelve euros a day.

notes.notes: In museums and on market stalls. 'Niet' + infinitive is the standard sign for 'do not ...'.

examples.tl: Bij het schilderij hangt een bordje: niet aanraken.
examples.en: There's a sign by the painting: do not touch.

notes.notes: On windows, fences and doors. Bikes left there can be removed: use a rack ('rek') or a 'fietsenstalling'.

examples.tl: Op het raam staat: hier geen fietsen plaatsen.
examples.en: The window says: no bike parking here.

notes.notes: On white plates under traffic signs: 'uitgezonderd fietsers' = except cyclists, so bikes may come the 'wrong' way.

examples.tl: Eenrichtingsverkeer, uitgezonderd fietsers.
examples.en: One-way traffic, except cyclists.

notes.notes: Short for 'alstublieft' on signs and notes: 'Deur sluiten a.u.b.', 'Niet storen a.u.b.' Read out as the full word.

examples.tl: Deur sluiten a.u.b.
examples.en: Please close the door.

notes.notes: Short for 'tot en met' in opening hours and dates: 'ma t/m vr' = Monday through Friday.

examples.tl: Geopend di t/m zo van 10.00 tot 17.00 uur.
examples.en: Open Tuesday through Sunday from 10 am to 5 pm.

notes.notes: On ticket machines ('kies uw bestemming') and on the front of trams and buses. Plural: bestemmingen.

examples.tl: Kies eerst uw bestemming op het scherm.
examples.en: First choose your destination on the screen.

notes.notes: The red button on ticket machines and card terminals. Green 'OK' or 'akkoord' confirms. Geannuleerd = cancelled.

examples.tl: Druk op 'annuleren' om opnieuw te beginnen.
examples.en: Press 'cancel' to start again.

notes.notes: On station signs next to 'lift' and 'roltrap' (escalator). Plural: trappen. Dutch house stairs are famously steep.

examples.tl: Neem de trap naar perron twee.
examples.en: Take the stairs to platform two.

notes.notes: Said 'mu-ZAY-um'. Plural: musea. Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum, Anne Frank Huis: book a time slot online.

examples.tl: Welk museum raadt u aan?
examples.en: Which museum do you recommend?

notes.notes: Plural: kerken. Oude Kerk, Westerkerk. Many old churches now serve as concert halls or museums.

examples.tl: De toren van de kerk kun je beklimmen.
examples.en: You can climb the church tower.

notes.notes: Plural: molens. See working ones at the Zaanse Schans and at Kinderdijk.

examples.tl: Bij de Zaanse Schans kun je een molen van binnen bekijken.
examples.en: At the Zaanse Schans you can see inside a windmill.

notes.notes: Plural: kastelen. Muiderslot near Amsterdam and De Haar near Utrecht are the easy day trips.

examples.tl: Het kasteel is alleen in het weekend open.
examples.en: The castle is only open at the weekend.

notes.notes: 'Gratis toegang' = free entry. Toegangsprijs = admission price. Also called 'entree'.

examples.tl: De toegang is gratis voor kinderen.
examples.en: Admission is free for children.

notes.notes: Said 'RONT-lay-ding'. Plural: rondleidingen. Gids = guide.

examples.tl: Is er een rondleiding in het Engels?
examples.en: Is there a guided tour in English?

notes.notes: A long one: ten-TOHN-stel-ling. Plural: tentoonstellingen. Special exhibitions often need a separate ticket.

examples.tl: De tentoonstelling over Rembrandt loopt tot januari.
examples.en: The Rembrandt exhibition runs until January.

notes.notes: Said 'skhil-duh-RAY'. Plural: schilderijen. De Nachtwacht (The Night Watch) hangs in the Rijksmuseum.

examples.tl: Dit schilderij is van Vermeer.
examples.en: This painting is by Vermeer.

notes.notes: Plural: foto's. 'Een foto maken' = to take a photo (you 'make' it).

examples.tl: Ik wil een foto van de gracht maken.
examples.en: I want to take a photo of the canal.

notes.notes: Plural: rondvaarten. Boats leave from in front of Centraal Station and along the Damrak.

examples.tl: De rondvaart door de grachten duurt een uur.
examples.en: The cruise through the canals takes an hour.

notes.notes: Said 'vayr'. Also an adverb meaning 'again'. The Buienradar app shows rain minute by minute.

examples.tl: Het weer is vandaag prachtig.
examples.en: The weather is gorgeous today.

notes.notes: Said 'RAY-khun'. 'Een bui' = a shower. Locals just cycle through it.

examples.tl: Er komt vanmiddag regen.
examples.en: Rain is coming this afternoon.

notes.notes: 'De zon schijnt' = the sun is shining. 'In de zon' = in the sun.

examples.tl: Zodra de zon schijnt, zit elk terras vol.
examples.en: As soon as the sun shines, every terrace is full.

notes.notes: Said 'vint'. Flat country: a headwind ('tegenwind') matters a lot on a bike or in a race.

examples.tl: Er staat veel wind aan de kust.
examples.en: It's very windy on the coast.

notes.notes: Said 'kowt'. 'Ik heb het koud' = I am cold (not 'ik ben koud').

examples.tl: Het is koud vandaag, neem een jas mee.
examples.en: It's cold today, bring a coat.

notes.notes: Covers warm and hot weather alike. 'Heet' is for very hot things, like soup.

examples.tl: Het is lekker warm in de zon.
examples.en: It's nice and warm in the sun.

notes.notes: For views, buildings, weather and things. 'Mooi weer' = nice weather.

examples.tl: Wat een mooie stad!
examples.en: What a beautiful city!

notes.notes: Plural: steden (irregular). 'De binnenstad' = the old centre. 'De stad in gaan' = to go into town.

examples.tl: Utrecht is een gezellige stad.
examples.en: Utrecht is a lively, friendly city.

notes.notes: Always plural. Posted on doors with day abbreviations: ma di wo do vr za zo.

examples.tl: De openingstijden staan op de website.
examples.en: The opening hours are on the website.

notes.notes: Plural: volwassenen. On price lists next to 'kinderen' (children) and '65+'.

examples.tl: Eén volwassene en twee kinderen, alstublieft.
examples.en: One adult and two children, please.

notes.notes: At a museum or boat ticket desk. The Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum are free for under-18s.

examples.tl: Twee volwassenen, alstublieft. — Dat is dan vijfenveertig euro.
examples.en: Two adults, please. — That comes to forty-five euros.

notes.tl: Hoe laat gaat het museum open?
notes.en: What time does the museum open?
